revision.title: SCAR: Test security fixes against the real exploit before they ship
revision.summary: A security fix can stop the published attack and still leave money exposed, or close the hole and break normal use. SCAR checks a fix the way an attacker would: it forks Ethereum at the block before a real exploit, runs that exploit against the patched contract, and confirms normal use still works. This grant pays for 24 reviewed Ethereum incident cases, a public scoreboard for AI-written fixes, and getting audit firms, bounty platforms and protocols to use the check.

sections.why:
Protocol users are safer from the second drain: the same exploit working again after the team says it is fixed.

- The Verus bridge on Ethereum lost about $11.5 million on 18 May 2026. Most of it was returned for a bounty and put back into the same bridge on 8 July. On 23 July it lost $7.54 million through the same contract path and bug class ([CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/07/23/bitcoin-ethereum-linked-protocols-lose-usd35-million-in-multiple-attacks-hours-apart)).
- TRM Labs counted a record 207 hacks in the first half of 2026, 125 of them exploiting smart-contract code ([TRM Labs](https://www.trmlabs.com/resources/blog/h1-2026-crypto-hacks-reach-record-high-as-losses-fall-below-usd-1-billion)).

Verus is why a fix gets re-tested before the money goes back in. After this grant, any team can run the exploit and the variants a reviewer would write against its own fix, and get a verdict anyone can re-run: solved, not solved or inconclusive.
sections.in_scope:
- **24 incident cases** on Ethereum mainnet or L2s with over $200 million secured on L2BEAT, 16 public and 8 private until the scoreboard freezes. Each has the real exploit on frozen chain state, a working reference fix, and two near-miss fixes (one incomplete, one that breaks normal use).
- **A workflow teams run themselves**: Foundry import, command line, CI job and coding-agent adapter.
- **A public scoreboard** grading AI agents' fixes on the private cases, with appeals.
- **Onboarding**: intake template, self-serve guide, and hands-on setup of each adopter's first two cases (fork, exploit and normal-use checks, reviewer sign-off).

Cost basis: one founder full time for 7 months on engineering, case building, onboarding and support ($45,000), 110 reviewer hours at $175 ($19,250), 12 exploit reproductions from outside contributors at $500 ($6,000), archive RPC, hosting and compute ($8,000), tools and bounties ($4,500), contingency ($7,250).
sections.out_scope:
- Proofs or whole-contract certification
- Build systems other than Foundry
- A hosted commercial service
- Retrieval and model-training research
- Chains other than Ethereum and its L2s
sections.team:
**Farseen Shaikh**, founder of SCAR AI, works on it full time (github.com/FarseenSh). In this fund's first round, SCAR received $6,275 (linked). Its open datasets, including a 231,269-contract Solidity corpus, have over 1,800 Hugging Face downloads (linked). SunSec (DeFiHackLabs) used SCAR's retrieval model in auditing and credited it with higher recall in a first-place OneSavie Bastet Kaggle entry (linked).

An independent reviewer, named in the grant agreement, signs off every case and milestone. No other funder pays for this scope; E2B and Daytona credits cover part of the compute.
sections.why_grant:
- **Fix Verifier** (Apache-2.0): replays four historical exploits on frozen chain state, one on Ethereum mainnet and three on BNB Chain, and grades a fix on security checks its author never sees, plus normal-use checks. CI re-grades every control fix.
- **48 published receipts** for control fixes we wrote to test the checker. 26 stop the replayed exploit, yet 15 of those still fail: they leave another path open or break normal use. A replay-only check passes all 15.
- **Revision checks**, previewed on four public OpenZeppelin and Safe changes: 10 of 10 valid versions accepted, 6 of 6 planted faults rejected.

What is thin: one Ethereum mainnet incident, and no outside reviewer or user of the verifier yet. The harness, receipts and CI exist, so this is not a from-scratch build.
sections.commitments:
- New code under Apache-2.0, case write-ups under CC BY 4.0; third-party material keeps its own terms.
- Farseen maintains the funded release for 6 months after the last milestone at no further cost; after that, revenue from paid checks and support pays for it.
- A verdict never says "safe" or "audited": it states what was replayed and checked, with inputs and a hash anyone can re-run.
- Confidential adopter material goes only to the reviewer.
- Private cases are published after the scoreboard freezes, with a tagged release.
- Pinned target: at least 4 outside organizations using the check on 8 real fixes.

milestones.name: 12 reviewed cases and an outside reproduction
criteria: At least 12 Ethereum mainnet or L2 cases (8 public, 4 private), each signed off by the technical reviewer, with receipts for the public ones
An engineer outside SCAR reproduces the workflow on a public case from the pinned commit, with the record in the repository

milestones.name: 24 cases and the public scoreboard
criteria: At least 24 cases signed off in total (16 public, 8 private), receipts published
The scoreboard grades at least 3 AI agents built on open models on the private cases with equal budgets, every result shown, with appeals
Intake template, reviewer archive and self-serve guide published on scarai.xyz

milestones.name: First outside team
criteria: At least 2 real fixes done and at least 1 of them not among SCAR's cases and 1 of the fixes for an outside organization with over $100 million onchain (token market cap or TVL) or one of OpenZeppelin, Trail of Bits, ChainSecurity, Spearbit, Consensys Diligence, Sigma Prime, Certora, Cyfrin, Zellic, Ackee Blockchain, Runtime Verification, Nethermind Security, Code4rena, Sherlock, Cantina, Immunefi, CodeHawks, HackenProof

milestones.name: Four teams and repeat use
criteria: At least 4 such organizations and 8 real fixes in total, at least 3 of the fixes not among SCAR's cases
Repeat Use: At least 2 of those organizations use SCAR again on a new fix 30 or more days after their first
A business plan for maintenance after the grant, and at least $5000 of revenue earned
